response.rationale: Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease is characterized by tender lymphadenopathy, fever, and necrotizing lymphadenitis with karyorrhexis and a lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate, fitting the vignette. Castleman disease and Rosai-Dorfman disease do not typically show coagulative necrosis with karyorrhexis.

rejected.why: Castleman disease typically shows hyaline-vascular or plasma cell changes without coagulative necrosis and karyorrhexis.
Rosai-Dorfman disease classically shows sinus histiocytosis with emperipolesis, not coagulative necrosis with karyorrhexis.
